text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd said it was recommending shares of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd as an accumulate investment, reflecting its possible exposure to a takeover if bank ownership rules are relaxed.
"ANZ is considered a possible target if bank ownership restrictions are relaxed. Cost savings will enhance future profit growth," analyst Greg Cathro said in a report.

Cathro told Reuters on Tuesday his recommendation for ANZ remained in force following Monday's announcement of a planned merger between regional players St George Bank Ltd and Advance Bank Australia Ltd.
"This will create even more interest in the banking sector and a lot can happen between now and April next year," he said.
Cathro said in a report that ANZ had a sound capital position without being over-capitalised.
"This is one reason for it not pursuing acquisitions or share buy-backs, preferring to pursue organic growth," he said.
ANZ had a strong Australian banking franchise and derived about 60 percent of profit domestically, he said.
The bank also had a diverse international network while in the domestic market there was a high exposure to small business lending, Cathro said.
"This should be an advantage with the housing market in the doldrums and extremely competitive," he said.
Cathro was forecasting ANZ net profits of A$1.05 billion for the year ended September 30, 1996 compared with a reported $953.6 million in 1994/95.
"Our forecast is for a relatively flat September 1996 half year and a modest profit increase in the folowing financial year," Cathro said.
"However the dividend payout ratio and dividend franking should rise to reward shareholders," he said.
Total dividends for the current year were forecast to rise to 37.5 cents (50 percent franked) and to 42.5 cents in 1996/97 which would be 100 percent franked.
The bank paid 33 cents a share total (18 percent franked) in the year ended September, 1995.
ANZ shares were trading five cents higher at A$7.39 in early trading on Tuesday.
